title: Gaits, Windows, Rolls, Wheels & Shaders
description: A solved walk cycle, windowed custom layouts, glyph reels, a drag-summoned drop wheel and a slider whose transitions are shaders.

drops.title: The Walk Is Solved, Not Keyframed
drops.description: Three ink figures walk on a procedural gait — no keyframes, the pose is recomputed every frame.
drops.concept: The planted foot is pinned to the ground and slides back at the body's travel speed; the swinging foot follows a minimum-jerk path with a lift arc; hip height falls out of what the standing leg can reach, so the body rises and dips over each step. Two-bone IK places the knees, the arms run as pendulums against the legs, and a single time-of-day value drives the whole palette from noon to midnight.
drops.source: JDhruv14/line-art-animation — animated line-art SVG figures with a gait solver and a day/night cycle

interaction.mouse: Drag speed, stride, ink weight and the hour; switch on Bones to see the joints the solver places.
interaction.click: Tap a figure and they tip their hat.
interaction.touch: Tapping works the same; the day cycle keeps running on its own.

drops.title: Write the Layout, Mount the Window
drops.description: Three hand-written layout functions over 2,000 items — and about 25 DOM nodes at a time.
drops.concept: A layout here is just a function: given a width and the items, return a frame per item plus a total height. Masonry, timeline and board are three of them. A separate windowing pass binary-searches the frames sorted by y, mounts only what the viewport plus overscan can see, and returns everything else to a node pool. Switch windowing off to mount all 2,000 and watch the frame counter answer for itself.
drops.source: Dave861/LazyLayoutKit — write your own layout and have it build only the views on screen

interaction.mouse: Scroll the list and watch the mounted-node count hold steady; switch layouts and tune the overscan.
interaction.click: Masonry, Timeline and Board swap the layout function; the windowing toggle mounts everything at once.
interaction.touch: Flick-scrolling recycles nodes the same way.

drops.title: Everything Rolls, Not Just Digits
drops.description: A glyph reel is a one-character window over a tape rebuilt for every change — so letters and shapes roll too.
drops.concept: On each change the reel builds a tape holding exactly the glyphs between the old value and the new one, jumps to the start with no transition, forces a reflow and then transitions to the end — so 7 → 2 really passes 8, 9, 0, 1. Only the columns that changed move, the stagger runs left to right, and once a roll settles the tape collapses back to a single glyph.
drops.source: cesarvenzac/roll — text that rolls as it changes: digits like an odometer, letters and icons rolling over

interaction.mouse: Tune duration, stagger and overshoot, or force the roll direction up or down.
interaction.click: Tap anywhere to roll the counter, the word, the shapes and the four tiles at once.
interaction.touch: Same tap; it also rolls on its own every few seconds.

drops.title: Drag First, Then Ask Where
drops.description: Start dragging a file and a wheel of drop targets fans out under the pointer, chosen by what you grabbed.
drops.concept: The menu is summoned by the drag rather than opened before it. Wedges are built per file type — a converter never offers the format you already have — and because the pointer is captured, selection is pure angle maths rather than hover. The caption shows the file's size until you reach a wedge, resting on More turns the page without closing the wheel, and release outside or Escape cancels.
drops.source: Manan-Santoki/OpenShelf — start dragging a file, tap a key, and drop it on a wheel of actions

interaction.mouse: Drag a file, move out to a wedge to select by angle, release to run it; shift, alt and ctrl swap the wheel mid-drag.
interaction.click: Arrow keys pick a wedge by keyboard, Enter runs it, Escape cancels.
interaction.touch: Touch-drag opens the same wheel; pick the wheel type from the panel on a larger screen.

drops.title: The Slider Is a Shader
drops.description: Real HTML slides in the document, one WebGL 2 canvas over the top, and transitions as swappable shader plugins.
drops.concept: Content, links and keyboard order stay in the markup; the GPU layer only draws the gap between two slides. Drag, flick, wheel and arrow keys all feed one spring that is stepped in small fixed slices, and five fragment-shader plugins — crossfade, liquid, glitch, dissolve and weave — read the same pair of textures. When the spring settles the render loop stops entirely, and with no WebGL 2 the real slides slide instead.
drops.source: niklasp/gpuslider — a slider drawn by shaders, with everything but the core as a plugin

interaction.mouse: Drag or flick to scrub, scroll to step, and tune stiffness, damping and snapping.
interaction.click: Pick an effect plugin or a dot; arrow keys and 1–5 jump between slides.
interaction.touch: Swipe to throw the spring; the shader draws the whole way.
